- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model underestimates prices during sustained downward trends (e.g., 75–77 range) — shows persistent bias toward lower values.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the middle of the 30-day window (days 10–20) — model struggles with mid-term volatility.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price movements — fails to adjust quickly to new data, especially after a spike or drop.
- When history includes a recent high, model often forecasts a lower value than true outcome — suggests underweighting recent momentum.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
- Forecasts are often too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the medium term (10–20 days) — exhibits asymmetric bias.
- Model fails to account for “recovery” or “rebound” after a sharp drop — often underestimates the return to prior levels.
- When true outcome shows a strong upward trend, model often underestimates the magnitude — especially if the trend is driven by policy or supply shocks.
